data.gender_notes: Magdeliah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Magdeliah is derived from the Hebrew words ‘magdhela’ which means ‘tower’ and ‘el’ which means ‘God’. This name is often associated with the biblical figure Mary Magdalene. In the New Testament, she is described as being present at Jesus' crucifixion and as the first person to see Jesus after his resurrection. The name Magdalene comes from Magdala, the ancient city on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee where she is believed to have lived.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of faith, devotion, and love.
data.etymology: Magdeliah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Majestic tower, or of Magdala.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Magdeliah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: מגדליה
in_hebrew.meaning: מגדליה - מי שגדל או מי שמעלה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מגדליה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'מי שגדל' או 'מי שמעלה'. השם מגיע מהשורש ג-ד-ל שפירושו 'להגדיל' או 'להעלאות'. השם קשור לנושא הרוחני של גדילה והתפתחות, והוא משמש כזכר ליכולת של אלוהים להעלות ולהגדיל את עמו.

in_greek.name: Μαγδελία
in_greek.long_meaning: Μαγδελία είναι ἕνα ὄνομα ἑβραϊκό, ποὺ σημαίνει 'Τού μεγαλοῦ' ἤ 'Τῆς μεγαλοψυχίας'. Τὸ ὄνομα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑβραϊκὴ λέξη מִגְדָּל (migdal), ποὺ σημαίνει 'πύργος' ἤ 'ὕψος'. Στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη, τὸ ὄνομα Μαγδαλή συνδέεται μὲ τὴν Μαρία Μαγδαληνή, μιὰ ἀπὸ τὶς σημαντικότερες γυναῖκες ποὺ ἀκολούθησαν τὸν Ἰησοῦ.

in_latin.name: Magdeliah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Magdeliah hebraicum est, quod significat 'qui crescit' vel 'qui exaltat'. Radix nominis est ג-ד-ל (g-d-l), quod significat 'crescere' vel 'exaltare'. Nomen hoc in traditione christiana significat incrementum et exaltationem spiritualem, reminiscentiam habens de potestate Dei elevandi et crescentis populum suum.

in_english.name: Magdeliah
in_english.meaning: Tower of God, Greatness of God, or Elevated One
in_english.long_meaning: The name Magdeliah originates from Hebrew roots, specifically from the word 'migdal,' meaning 'tower' or 'elevated place.' It is associated with spiritual growth, elevation, and greatness. The name may relate to the biblical figure Mary Magdalene, one of Jesus' closest followers. In Christian tradition, Magdeliah symbolizes spiritual ascension and the pursuit of divine greatness.

celebrity_usage: Mary Magdalene (character in The Last Supper)
data.cultural_impact: The name Magdeliah has a rich history with Christian tradition. Mary Magdalene is a significant figure in Christianity, typically identified as a repentant sinner and a follower of Jesus. Her memory has been a source of inspiration for Christian art, literature, and music. The name Magdeliah, carries the legacy of this influential woman, and is used as a name that signifies strength, resilience, and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, Mary Magdalene is a powerful symbol of repentance, transformation, and faith. Her story of being present at Jesus' crucifixion, witnessing his resurrection, and being the first to spread the good news of his resurrection, serves as a reminder of the transformative power of faith and the importance of staying committed to it. The name Magdeliah is a powerful reminder that no matter our past, we can always turn to God for forgiveness, healing, and strength.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Magdaliah is a variant of the biblical name Mary Magdalene, symbolizing transformation and redemption. She is remembered as a penitent sinner who became a devoted follower of Jesus Christ. Magdaliah's name embodies the spiritual journey from sin to salvation.

historical_references.reference: The Synoptic Gospels (Matthew, Mark, and Luke) recount a woman named Mary Magdalene who was present at Jesus' crucifixion and burial and was the first to see Jesus resurrected. This Mary is also sometimes referred to as ‘Mary of Magdala’ or ‘Madeleine’ in French, and her modern English name is often ‘Mary Magdalene’.
historical_references.context: New Testament of the Christian Bible

historical_references.reference: In medieval Europe, the legend of Mary Magdalene was conflated with that of the repentant sinner, Mary of Bethany, who anointed Jesus’ feet with expensive perfume in the Gospel of Luke. As a result, Mary Magdalene came to be associated with penance and sexual redemption. This association is reflected in the naming of many churches, convents, and schools dedicated to her throughout Europe.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Magdeliah, derived from the biblical figure Mary Magdalene, has gained popularity in modern culture as a symbol of self-care, inspiration, and mental health. On Instagram, users often use the hashtag #Magdeliah as a way to share their self-care routines and encourage others to prioritize their wellbeing. Pinterest boards dedicated to Magdeliah showcase images of peaceful gardens, calming colors, and quotes meant to inspire and uplift. Blogs and articles about Magdeliah focus on the importance of introspection, healing, and self-love, often drawing on the metaphor of Magdeliah's journey from being a sinner to a penitent and eventually becoming a beloved disciple of Jesus. Overall, Magdeliah is seen as a modern symbol of transformation, resilience, and self-discovery.
